summary: A letter-style note from people at Atomic Energy Commission sites, including Argonne, Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory and New York University, who were planning to join the ARPANET. They needed remote job entry (RJE) early, and propose a lightweight way to do it over FTP, using reserved pathname conventions such as RJE.JOB, RJE.PR and RJE.STAT, instead of implementing a separate RJE protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 551 proposes using FTP to send jobs to remote computers and retrieve their output. It lets sites reuse file transfer instead of implementing a separate remote job-entry protocol.

subtitle: A proposal to submit remote computer jobs through FTP.

tldr.problem: Three Atomic Energy Commission sites planned to join the ARPANET and needed remote job entry. They wanted to avoid implementing a separate job-entry protocol.
tldr.mechanism: The proposal assigns special FTP pathnames to job submission, output retrieval and status requests. Site-specific control cards in the transferred file provide job parameters.
tldr.outcome: RFC 551 proposes a way to use FTP for remote job entry; it does not define a common job-execution protocol.

today: RFC 551 is a historical proposal for using FTP pathnames to support remote job entry at sites joining the ARPANET.

sections.title: Why the Sites Needed Remote Job Entry
sections.content: Argonne National Laboratory, Lawrence Berkeley Labs and New York University were planning to join the network. Their applications made remote job entry, or RJE, an early need, but the sites wanted to avoid implementing a separate RJE protocol in addition to FTP.
sections.plainLanguage: Three laboratories planned to join the network and needed to run jobs on remote computers. They wanted to use FTP, which they already expected to implement, rather than build another protocol.

sections.title: FTP Pathnames for Jobs and Output
sections.content:
The proposal uses site-dependent FTP pathname conventions. A STOR request for a pathname beginning with RJE.JOB queues the transferred file for execution. RJE.PR, RJE.PU and RJE.MT identify print, punch and magtape output; RJE.STAT requests a status file through RETR.

Job parameters are not part of the protocol. The sender includes them in the site's standard control cards, which also determine output handling.
sections.plainLanguage: A special FTP pathname tells the remote site whether a transfer is a job, output or status request. The site's control cards, sent with the job, specify how it runs and where its output goes.

sections.title: What FTP Handles
sections.content:
The FTP login, account and password validate the data transfer and help identify and distribute output. They do not decide whether the submitted job is authorized to run. The RFC describes local pathname conventions, not a shared mechanism for job permissions or execution parameters.

The authors invite comments on problems they may have overlooked.
sections.plainLanguage: FTP credentials check the transfer and help route its output. They do not grant permission to execute a job; each site handles job details through its own conventions.
